title: Giving to the church
hook: supporting the community that supports you
tomorrow: what do you pray for a church that isn't yours?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: hands needed, tables and the word in one family of serving. Today, the part people get awkward about: money.

First paycheck, and before it's even spent, everyone has an opinion: save it, treat yourself, give some away. How much goes to church, if any? In today's letters, Paul never names a number. He names something else: a partnership. A church may sing about heaven, but it lives on earth, with a light bill and a roof, and Paul writes about paying for it openly, and with a lot of thanks.
screen: `FIRST PAYCHECK.` → `HOW MUCH, IF ANY?` → `NOT A NUMBER: A PARTNERSHIP.`

segments.voice: Start with Galatians: “Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.” Communicate, in the old English, means share. Teaching flows one way; support flows back. Then Philippi. Paul, in chains, remembers a church that kept sending help: “no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.” Their gift came by the hand of Epaphroditus, and Paul doesn't call it a fee. He calls it “an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.” Money, given to the work, became worship. Nobody shamed them into it; they gave as partners. Churches answer the how-much differently. Some teach the tithe; some ask each person to decide in their own heart; time and skill count too. Now a neighbor. Sikhs read a line of Guru Nanak in the Guru Granth Sahib: the one who earns by honest work and gives some of what he has, he is the one who knows the path. Christians and Sikhs share this: giving belongs inside an ordinary working life, not only in grand gestures. And one honest difference. Paul frames the gift as a share in a church's work, offered to God like a sacrifice. Guru Nanak's line sets giving beside honest work, as part of the path itself.
screen: `TAUGHT, SO SHARE.` · `A SWEET SMELL, NOT A FEE.` · `HOW MUCH? CHURCHES DIFFER.` · `GURU NANAK: EARN HONESTLY, GIVE.` · then, large: `SUPPORT IT.`

segments.voice: Name one gift, any size, for a church or community that has fed you: some money, an hour, a skill. Name what might get in the way, then the one step that gets it there. If you pray, offer it to God as a share, not a fee.
Giving to the church. Sharing money, time or skill with the community that teaches and holds you, as a partner in its work.
Your line: support it. Paul called that gift wellpleasing to God. That's day seventeen forty-nine.

chat.says: first paycheck! pop says give a tenth to church. nia says give it to the pantry. who's right??
options: Churches differ on how much. Paul's point: share in the work that feeds you.
Pop. Paul set the rule: exactly a tenth, or it doesn't count.
Nia. Giving to a church is basically a fee, so the pantry wins.
chat.meaning: Paul calls the Philippians' gift a share, wellpleasing to God, not a fee. Churches teach the amount differently; partnership is the point.

Language claim (trapdoor, original): 'communicate' in Galatians 6:6 and Philippians 4:15 renders the Greek koinoneo. Confirm accents and sound-out.

'Nobody shamed them into it; they gave as partners' keeps the earlier line that a church that pressures or shames is not doing what Paul describes. Confirm tone.

A Sikh reviewer should confirm the Ang, the attribution to Guru Nanak and the paraphrase. Honest difference stated without ranking: Paul frames the gift as a share in a church's work offered to God like a sacrifice; Guru Nanak's line sets giving beside honest work as part of the path. The fork's 'gurdwara and its free kitchen' describes a coworker's practice; dasvandh and its customary share are deliberately not named, to avoid an unsourced number.
